review.brief_reason: The original contains log(sqrt(x3)) inside the inner sqrt, while the proposed replaces it with log(x3)/2. Under gplearn protected semantics, log(a)=log(abs(a)) when abs(a)>0.001 else 0, and sqrt(a)=sqrt(abs(a)). For x3=0.0001: original log(sqrt(0.0001))=log(0.01)=log(0.01)≈-4.605; proposed log(0.0001)/2≈-4.605. These happen to coincide here. But for x3=0.00005: sqrt(0.00005)≈0.00707, abs>0.001 so log(sqrt(x3))=log(0.00707)≈-4.954; proposed log(0.00005)/2≈-4.954. Still same. The real issue: for x3 with abs(x3)<=0.001, log(x3) returns 0 (protected), but log(sqrt(x3)) also returns 0 since abs(sqrt(x3))<=0.001. So they match in protected regime too. However, the expressions are NOT algebraically identical in general because log(sqrt(x3)) = (1/2)*log(x3) only when sqrt(x3)>0.001 AND x3>0.001 simultaneously. For x3 in (0.000001, 0.001): sqrt(x3) ranges from 0.001 to 0.0316, so for x3=0.000001, sqrt=0.001, log(sqrt)=log(0.001)≈-6.908; but log(x3)=0 (protected, abs(x3)<0.001), so log(x3)/2=0. Counterexample: x3=0.0005, x0=1.0.
review.counterexample: x3=0.0005, x0=1.0: original has log(sqrt(0.0005))=log(0.02236)≈-3.802 (abs(0.02236)>0.001 so protected log applies); proposed has log(0.0005)/2=0/2=0 (abs(0.0005)<0.001 so protected log returns 0). These differ, changing the inner sqrt argument and thus the entire expression value.
